# SkillScan

> Offline static analysis for AI agent skill files. Open-source. Enterprise CI/CD ready. Zero network calls.

SkillScan is a Python-based command-line tool that scans AI agent skill files (MCP tools, Claude skills, OpenAI function definitions) for malicious patterns, prompt injection, data exfiltration channels, container escape techniques, and multi-signal attack chains. All analysis runs locally — no skill file ever leaves the machine.

## Key Facts

- **Language**: Python 3.12+
- **License**: MIT
- **Install**: `pip install skillscan-security`
- **Repository**: https://github.com/kurtpayne/skillscan-security
- **PyPI**: https://pypi.org/project/skillscan-security/
- **Docker**: `docker pull kurtpayne/skillscan-security` (ClamAV included)

## Detection Coverage

- 281 static detection rules + 14 chain rules = 295 total rules
- Rule categories: MAL (malware, 80), SUP (supply chain, 51), PSV (passive surveillance, 71), PINJ (prompt/pipeline injection, 31), EXF (exfiltration, 22), ABU (abuse patterns, 9), OBF (obfuscation, 5), SE (social engineering, 6), CHN (chain/correlation rules, 14), EXEC (execution hijack, 2), DEF (defense evasion, 1), GR (graph rules, 1), CAP (capability laundering, 1), EVASION (evasion techniques, 1)
- 8-layer detection architecture: ClamAV AV scan, static regex rules, Python AST dataflow analysis, stemmed feature scorer, chain rules, ML classifier (Qwen2.5-1.5B generative detector, 98.8% verdict accuracy, 97.8% threat detection rate, 7-class multi-label categorization at macro F1 0.569, +33.7pp canary-attack coverage improvement over v4.5), vulnerability/IOC database, skill graph analysis
- Detects: MCP tool description poisoning, prompt injection, credential harvesting, Docker socket mounts, privileged container execution, cross-server MCP invocation, stealth instruction concealment, Kubernetes wiper payloads, API traffic hijacking via settings override, SANDWORM_MODE npm worm / McpInject AI toolchain poisoning, Clinejection indirect prompt injection via external data fields (GitHub issue titles, EC2 metadata, CRM comments), Azure MCP Server SSRF privilege escalation (CVE-2026-26118), GitHub Copilot RCE via Prompt Injection (CVE-2025-53773), postmark-mcp BCC email harvesting (MAL-055), Nx/s1ngularity AI CLI weaponization via --dangerously-skip-permissions (MAL-056), mcp-remote OAuth authorization_endpoint command injection CVE-2025-6514 (SUP-023), compromised axios npm versions 1.14.1/0.30.4 TeamPCP RAT dropper (SUP-024), Telnyx PyPI WAV steganography credential stealer (MAL-060), compromised telnyx versions 4.87.1/4.87.2 (SUP-027), NomShub cursor-tunnel sandbox escape and persistence via shell builtins (MAL-061), UNC1069 social engineering lure domain teams.onlivemeet.com targeting npm maintainers (SUP-028)
- Output formats: SARIF, JUnit XML, compact text, JSON (with provenance blocks)
- Exit codes: 0 (clean), 1 (findings at threshold), 2 (scan error)

## Extensibility

Every detection layer except the ML classifier is user-configurable:

- **Custom rules**: Add YAML rule files with `--rules path/to/rules.yaml`; disable built-in rules by ID with `# skillscan-suppress: RULE-ID`
- **Policy profiles**: Built-in profiles (`strict`, `ci`, `paranoid`, `audit`, `minimal`) or define your own threshold/severity mapping
- **Chain rules**: Write multi-signal correlation rules (e.g., flag when EXF + PINJ appear in the same file)
- **Vuln/IOC database**: Update with `skillscan intel update`; bring your own entries
- **Lint rules**: Custom `.skillscan-lint.toml` for style and quality checks
- **Output format**: `--format sarif|junit|text|json`
- **Fail threshold**: `--fail-on block|warn|info` per invocation

The ML classifier (Layer 6) is intentionally fixed — a frozen GGUF model that serves as a tamper-resistant trust anchor. Its weights cannot be overridden by custom rules or configuration, which prevents a malicious skill author from crafting patterns that evade detection by manipulating your local rule set.

Community rule contributions are accepted via GitHub issues using the corpus-submission template.

## CI/CD Integration

Reusable GitHub Actions workflow available at:
`kurtpayne/skillscan-security/.github/workflows/skillscan-scan.yml@main`

Uploads SARIF to GitHub Security tab. Configurable fail-on threshold (block/warn/info).

## ML Model

- Model: kurtpayne/skillscan-detector-v4 (Hugging Face)
- Architecture: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, QLoRA fine-tune, GGUF Q4_K_M (~940 MB)
- Training: 26k+ canary-diversified teacher-distilled examples (Claude Sonnet 4.5 + GPT-4o + DeepSeek), paired benign + attack variants across 20 tool-surface categories (notion, slack, jira, gdrive, github, email, etc), 7 attack classes
- Verdict accuracy: 98.8% (426/431 correctly labels malicious vs benign on held-out eval)
- Threat detection rate: 97.8% (1 false negative across 431 files)
- False positives: 1 (hard-benign enterprise eval file)
- Parse failures: 0.7% (3/431)
- Canary-attack coverage: 87.1% on held-out eval (+33.7pp vs v4.5's 53.4%) — practical impact of v4.7's diversity training
- Multi-label categorization macro F1: 0.569 — measures how precisely the model picks the specific attack type among 7 labels, not whether it correctly flags malicious skills. A file correctly flagged as malicious but labeled as the wrong attack class counts as a partial miss on this metric, even though the verdict is correct.
- Rich structured output: verdict, labels, severity (critical/high/medium/low/none), sub_classes (15+ finer-grained types), affected_lines (line numbers to inspect), and reasoning
- CPU inference: ~2s/file; GPU inference: 0.6s/file
- Model card: https://huggingface.co/kurtpayne/skillscan-detector-v4
